reason: The text demonstrates strict hierarchy throughout multiple levels: (1) Paternal authority - Jacob makes final decisions for his family and controls whether his sons can return to Egypt; (2) Governmental hierarchy - Joseph is explicitly described as 'הַשַּׁלִּ֣יט עַל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ' (the ruler over the land) and exercises absolute control; (3) Social hierarchy - Joseph's brothers repeatedly 'וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־ ל֥וֹ אַפַּ֖יִם אָֽרְצָה' (prostrate themselves before him), demonstrating respect for strict rank; (4) Power dynamics - Joseph speaks 'קָשׁ֗וֹת' (harshly) to his brothers from his position of authority, imprisons Simeon, and orchestrates all events. The narrative consistently emphasizes Joseph's role as ruler and demonstrates that strict hierarchy is both important and deeply embedded in the social structure.
